factions.speechStyle: short sentences, weather words, never says no directly
leaderBackstory: Ilse Marr was the well's third keeper and the first who could read the old pump manuals.
She rang the bell the night the sea died, and she has kept the rope in her hand ever since - even now that the bell only clanks.
broadcasts: Bellwell to all roads: water at the rope, news at the gate. Bring both.
No bell again tonight. The pans are quiet. Quiet is not the same as safe.
Wind from the ridge, dust on the pans. Keep your tanks closed and your eyes open.

lines: Bellwell to all roads: the bell speaks again. Caravans, you know the way.
Water came on the third day, the way it used to. Thank the ones who brought the bronze home.

history.headline: A TOWN THAT WAITS FOR A SOUND
history.subhead: How the Bell Folk kept a well alive on a dead sea.

sections.title: What the old world ran on
sections.body: Salt, shipping and a canal nobody finished. When the canal failed the sea drank itself dry in eleven summers, and the ships stayed where the water left them.

sections.title: Why a bell
sections.body: Radios need batteries. A bell needs one strong arm. For three generations the water caravans followed its note across the pans - and when it cracked, they stopped coming.

sections.title: The Saltmen
sections.body: Raiders who live out on the white, where nobody else can. They took the town's bronze reserve last winter and call it salvage.

people.name: Maren Kett
people.note: The founder's daughter. The town would follow her into the pans.

contracts.pitch: A mail bag for the scouts on the ridge. Don't read it. Everyone reads it.

factions.speechStyle: slow, amused, royal 'we', talks about thirst like a tax
leaderBackstory: Oszkar was a harbour pilot when there was still a harbour. He knows every sandbar that turned into a salt ridge.
He crowned himself with a porthole ring the day the last ship ran aground, and nobody on the white has argued since.
broadcasts: This is the Salt King. The white belongs to us. You may cross it. You may not keep what you carry.
We hear Bellwell counts its barrels now. We count them too.
Bronze does not rot and does not drink. We are keeping it safe for you, little well.

lines: The King is silent tonight. The white is not.
You took our bronze. Salt remembers.
